blocs.texte: Pour raconter des événements passés, on utilise le prétérit simple (past simple). Il sert à décrire une action terminée à un moment précis du passé.

Verbes réguliers : base verbale + ED (play → played, watch → watched). Verbes irréguliers : forme à apprendre par cœur (go → went, see → saw, have → had). Négation : did not (didn't) + base verbale. Question : Did + sujet + base verbale ?

lignes: la semaine / le mois / l'année dernière

blocs.texte: Last year, I went on a school trip to Antsirabe. It was an amazing experience. We visited a lake and took a lot of pictures. On the first day, the weather was wonderful, but on the second day, it rained and we had to stay at the hotel, which was quite boring. Overall, it was a memorable trip that I will never forget.

blocs.enonce: Raconte en 5 phrases minimum un événement passé mémorable (une sortie, un voyage, une fête...) en utilisant le prétérit simple et au moins 3 adjectifs descriptifs de la liste de vocabulaire.
blocs.solution: Réponse modèle : Last month, I went to my cousin's wedding in Fianarantsoa. It was a wonderful celebration. We danced all night and ate delicious food. The music was exciting and everyone was happy. It was truly an unforgettable day.

blocs.texte: On utilise 'used to' et 'would' pour parler d'habitudes ou de situations passées qui n'existent plus aujourd'hui.

Used to : sujet + used to + base verbale (pour des habitudes ET des états passés). Exemple : She used to live in Toamasina. Would : sujet + would + base verbale (seulement pour des habitudes répétées, PAS pour des états). Exemple : Every summer, we would visit our grandparents. Négation : didn't use to + base verbale. Question : Did + sujet + use to + base verbale ?

When Sarah was a child, she used to live in a small village with her grandparents. Every morning, she would wake up early and help her grandmother feed the chickens. She used to walk three kilometres to school every day because there was no bus. In the evenings, she would sit with her grandfather and listen to his stories about the old days. She didn't use to have a television, so the family would talk and play games together. Now Sarah lives in the city and things are very different, but she still remembers those simple days with happiness.

blocs.enonce: D'après le texte sur Sarah, réponds par Vrai ou Faux : 1) Sarah used to live in a big city. 2) She would walk to school. 3) She used to have a television at home. 4) Her grandfather used to tell her stories.
blocs.solution: 1) Faux (elle vivait dans un petit village). 2) Vrai. 3) Faux (elle n'avait pas de télévision). 4) Vrai.

blocs.enonce: Transforme ces phrases en utilisant 'used to' ou 'would' selon le cas (attention : 'would' ne peut pas être utilisé pour les états) : 1) I had long hair when I was young. 2) We played football every weekend. 3) She was afraid of the dark. 4) They visited their aunt every summer.
blocs.solution: 1) I used to have long hair when I was young. (état → used to uniquement) 2) We used to play / would play football every weekend. 3) She used to be afraid of the dark. (état → used to uniquement) 4) They used to visit / would visit their aunt every summer.

blocs.texte: Pour parler de ses dernières vacances, on utilise le prétérit et des questions en Wh- (Where, When, Who, What, How) pour poser des questions précises.

Rose: Hi Anna! Where did you go for your last vacation? Anna: I went to Nosy Be with my family. Rose: That sounds great! When did you go there? Anna: We went there in December, during the Christmas holidays. Rose: Who did you go with? Anna: I went with my parents and my little brother. Rose: What did you do there? Anna: We swam in the sea, visited the lemur park, and ate a lot of fresh seafood. Rose: How did you travel there? Anna: We travelled by plane from Antananarivo. It was a short but wonderful trip!

blocs.enonce: En t'inspirant du dialogue entre Anna et Rose, écris un court dialogue sur tes propres dernières vacances en utilisant au moins les 5 questions suivantes : Where...? When...? Who...? What...? How...?
blocs.solution: Réponse modèle : A: Where did you go for your last vacation? B: I went to Mahajanga. A: When did you go there? B: I went there in August. A: Who did you go with? B: I went with my cousins. A: What did you do there? B: We went to the beach and visited the baobab trees. A: How did you travel there? B: We travelled by bus.

blocs.texte: Les adjectifs positifs et négatifs permettent d'exprimer une opinion forte sur une expérience. On les utilise souvent dans des phrases exclamatives pour insister.

blocs.titre: Les structures exclamatives What a / How
blocs.texte: What + a/an + adjectif + nom (au singulier) ! Exemple : What a wonderful day! What + adjectif + noms (au pluriel ou indénombrables) ! Exemple : What beautiful flowers! How + adjectif (sans nom) ! Exemple : How amazing!
1) The food was terrible. → What terrible food! / How terrible! 2) The view was superb. → What a superb view! / How superb! 3) The movie was awful. → What an awful movie! / How awful!

blocs.enonce: Transforme ces phrases en phrases exclamatives avec 'What a/an' ou 'How' : 1) The party was fantastic. 2) The weather was dreadful. 3) The concert was lovely. 4) The exam was horrible.
blocs.solution: 1) What a fantastic party! / How fantastic! 2) What dreadful weather! / How dreadful! 3) What a lovely concert! / How lovely! 4) What a horrible exam! / How horrible!

blocs.texte: On utilise 'So' pour exprimer un accord avec une phrase affirmative, et 'Neither' (ou 'Nor') pour exprimer un accord avec une phrase négative.

Accord positif : So + auxiliaire + sujet. Exemple : I like tea. - So do I. Accord négatif : Neither/Nor + auxiliaire + sujet. Exemple : I don't like coffee. - Neither do I. L'auxiliaire doit correspondre au temps de la phrase d'origine (do/does/did, am/is/are/was/were, have/has/had, can/will/would...).

lignes: Neither do I. (si négatif : I don't play)

blocs.enonce: Réponds en utilisant 'So' ou 'Neither' selon le cas : 1) A: I love chocolate. B: ... 2) A: I don't like spiders. B: ... 3) A: She can speak French. B (he can too): ... 4) A: They haven't finished their homework. B (same): ...
blocs.solution: 1) So do I. 2) Neither do I. 3) So can he. 4) Neither have they / Neither has he (selon le sujet utilisé).

blocs.texte: Les mots de liaison de contraste permettent d'opposer deux idées dans une phrase.

Although / though / even though / even if / much as / whereas / while sont suivis d'une proposition complète (sujet + verbe conjugué). Despite et in spite of sont suivis d'un nom ou d'un verbe en -ing (PAS d'une proposition complète). Exemple incorrect : Despite he was tired... Exemple correct : Despite being tired, he finished the race. / Despite the rain, we went out.

1) Although it was raining, they went for a walk. 2) Despite the rain, they went for a walk. 3) In spite of being poor, the family was happy. 4) She passed the exam, whereas her brother failed it. 5) Even though he studied hard, he didn't pass the test.

blocs.enonce: Relie les deux idées avec le mot de liaison indiqué entre parenthèses : 1) He is young. He is very wise. (although) 2) The weather was bad. We had a picnic. (despite) 3) She likes maths. Her sister hates it. (whereas) 4) He failed the exam. He worked hard. (even though)
blocs.solution: 1) Although he is young, he is very wise. 2) Despite the bad weather, we had a picnic. 3) She likes maths, whereas her sister hates it. 4) Even though he worked hard, he failed the exam.
